title: Gone in the Wind
subtitle: The soil is moist and fertile in the south, where the song of the wind reaches far.

trails.title: Hygiene Guide
trails.description: For hostesses, cleanliness is next to godliness. Fortunately, the subject this hostess wishes to clean is all for it.

content.text:
Week 4
Routine Cleaning
Room 105: Cleaned carpet stained with vomit.
Room 108: Cleaned stains and fingerprints off walls.
Room 205: Broken glass, contacted supplier for replacement.

Week 5
Routine Cleaning
Room 105: Cleaned carpet stained with vomit. A lesson needs to be taught.
Room 211: Replaced showerhead.
Cracks in the glass in room 205 disappeared?

Week 8
Routine Cleaning
Front desk: Table needs repair.
Room 102: Floor scorched—I saw that, I'm sure of it.
Scorch marks disappeared. That's a good baby.

Week 10
Routine Cleaning
Room 105: Bloodstains, carpet ruined. It's time for punishment.
Room 202: Glass completely shattered.
Repaired all by itself. An good baby deserves a reward.
Tonight.
Room 105, of course.

trails.title: Sweet Dreams
trails.description: A song drifting through countless nights' dreams.

content.text:
Close your eyes, close your eyes, my darling little dear,
The shining moon and peaceful night are dancing ever near,
In your cradle, dream a dream, so tender and so sweet,
Dream a dream to entertain and make this night complete.

Close your eyes, close your eyes, my darling little one,
The owls have caught some squirrels, dear, such luck and oh such fun,
One by one, their eyes survey, on branches perched so high,
Feasting freely, oh such delight, their banquet in the sky.

Close your eyes, close your eyes, my darling little star,
The black horse roams the wilderness, through rolling fields afar,
Don't you fret, don't you fear, their hooves no harm shall bring,
Their gentle pitter-patter prances lighter than the wind.

Close your eyes, close your eyes, my darling little love,
The barn is filled with fright and fear, below as is above,
Breakfast ready, maws agape, a rousing sweet delight,
Here awaits you to awake, devoured by morning's light.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: What's going on?
Outside the motel, the rising dawn paints the earth a deep orange. Lilya looks confused as they approach.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Are you okay, Captain?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'm fine.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I have good news and bad news.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Don't bother with the order; just lay it on me.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The good news is we've found Barbara.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The bad news is we've got a new problem. This motel is the manifestation of a living consciousness that constantly generates urban legends and spreads fear. It might turn into a supernatural arcanist in the future.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We can't let it grow here unchecked. We need the help of the Foundation to keep it under control.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Boss, my job here is done. I'm heading into town for Kayla.
She looks off into the distance.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Oh, and I promised a young fella that I'd help him find his mother.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: I've gotta go now.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: How do I pay your fee?

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Fee?
She laughs heartily.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: We're friends, Vertin. I don't need no payment.
She says her goodbyes and sets off on the road ahead.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Alright, Captain, any progress on finding Urd?
The little sheep's ears twitch.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: That's why you came looking for me, right?

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: I'll ask the wind for you. It's the least I can do.
She closes her eyes.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Did she doze off?
The gentle breeze caresses her ears, like an invisible thread being woven between them.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: I'm listening.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: Oh, I heard it. The answer.
She opens her eyes.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: A distant wind told me that Ms. Urd's latest submission came from the São Paulo Veterans' Residence.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: The article she submitted was an excellent piece, but UTTU doesn't know anything beyond that.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Okay.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: I suppose we'll all have restful sleep and sweet dreams tonight.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: I've collected the material I needed for the upcoming feature interview. I bet the readers will enjoy it.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: I'll be sure to include your name on the byline, Ms. Tuesday.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Me? I don't think I contributed anything.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: Quite the contrary, you played a significant role. If it weren't for you, I wouldn't have realized my inner fear of losing communication with the world.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: First-hand experiences like this are invaluable to an editor.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Oh, with the way you put it, I almost regret letting you go.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: I won't be returning. The interview's over.
She closes her little red notebook.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: If all goes well, you'll be able to read about it in the next issue of UTTU.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: I'll take my leave now.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Goodbye.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Good, I can't wait to leave this place.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We can't leave yet.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I just contacted the Texas branch. Their staff is on their way here. They have to investigate this supernatural being as soon as possible.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: And they'll be here soon, I presume?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I can feel the energy fluctuations of teleportation rituals. It must be them.
She turns her head to see a stranger standing before her.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Mm?
The girl in front of her has chestnut hair and carries a woven basket on her arm.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Looks like you guessed wrong, Captain. I met her in town. Name's Kayla.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Kayla?
The girl smiles brightly at her.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Do you know someone called Argus?
The girl's smile becomes more gentle.

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: The name doesn't ring a bell. How strange! What kind of parent would name their child after a one-hundred-eyed giant?

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: You must've mistaken me for someone else. Kayla is a common name, after all, like Emma, Anna, or Catherine. More importantly, Miss, you look ...
The girl smiles once more.

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: Although I've never met you before, you seem familiar.
She reaches into the basket and pulls out a crumpled flower.
A pale moth lands on a petal, gently fluttering its wings, its scales shimmering in the morning light.

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: I hope you have a wonderful day.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Thank you.
The girl tucks the flower under her arm.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Are you a guest at this motel?
The girl nods.

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: What happened here?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The St. Pavlov Foundation has taken over. I suggest you find alternative accommodation, given the dangerous incidents that have occurred here.

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: Hmm. What should I do? All my things are still inside.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The Foundation staff will take care of it for you later. You can trust them.

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: Can't I just go and get my things now?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I would advise you to wait until the Foundation staff arrive.

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: Oh, I can look after myself. No need to worry about me, Miss.
The girl winks and pushes open the motel door, promptly disappearing from their view.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: That girl ...
Lilya breaks her long silence.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What about her?

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Never mind. It's probably nothing.
The light from a teleportation disk flickers nearby.

items.speaker: Foundation Staff I
items.text: Apologies for our delayed arrival, Ms. Vertin.

items.speaker: Foundation Staff I
items.text: We'd been unable to locate the motel until about ten minutes ago. It's as if something was deliberately interfering with our sense of direction.
While the Foundation staff is busy assessing the situation, a faint sound echoes from the depths of the motel.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Oh.
The door suddenly swings open, and a pale, trash-covered corpse is thrown out of it.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Once again, it insisted on eating garbage off the floor. Is every child this stubborn?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's Stefen, a Zeno officer.

items.speaker: Foundation Staff I
items.text: Hmm, Stefen. Sounds familiar.
The staff member flips through his records, quickly finding the information he's looking for.

items.speaker: Foundation Staff I
items.text: The records show he was a high-ranking Zeno officer who went missing after the vacuum bomb footage leaked.

items.speaker: Foundation Staff I
items.text: Zeno issued a staggering bounty on him. I guess whatever he did really angered Admiral Igor.

items.speaker: Foundation Staff I
items.text: Who would've thought he'd be hiding in this little motel in the middle of nowhere?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Obviously, luck wasn't on his side.

items.speaker: Foundation Staff I
items.text: Alright, Ms. Vertin, we'll take over from here.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: The maid remains calm, gently patting the bundle in her arms.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: After the branch completes its procedures, you'll be sent to the headquarters for a more thorough assessment.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Will you return my baby to me?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's too early to discuss that.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Let's go, Lilya.
She picks up the suitcase.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We must report back to Madam Z about Urd.
